construction_requirements.description: sōna swā temporal clause containing a geseah + ðæt finite content clause; supply complete relation, not only words.
habban with an object/relative referent and tō+inflected infinitive: have something available to offer/give; neither obligation nor generalized possession auxiliary.
Object-relative ðe and definite headless relative ðæt; no independent relative formation or mood task.
Accompanying present participle cweðende, with ðus; no finite ending or command.
Each source prepositional phrase supplied locally; neither familiar headword nor motion makes its government previously taught.
Wolde plus plain infinitive: volition, not automatic future-in-the-past; lexical infinitive gecȳðan remains supplied.
Nim and gā are direct second-singular imperatives. No PP imperative extension.
Tō + inflected infinitive morphology; source availability frame supplied separately.
Sealde with accusative gift and dative recipient; source nouns supplied.
Same fisherman subject continued without a repeated pronoun; local translation support supplies subject.

support_groups.local_meaning: Then, as soon as the fisherman saw that the young man was lying at his feet.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply the whole temporal frame and embedded content clause, with geonga/fiscere/fōtum/æt. His feet contextually refers to the fisherman. Familiar finite indicatives do not make either subordinate construction taught.
Supply mid mildheortnesse as manner and the prefixed verb ūpāhōf. Hē is the fisherman; hine is Apollonius.

support_groups.local_meaning: And led him with him to his house.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply mid him accompaniment and tō his hūse destination. Hine is Apollonius; him and his contextually refer to the fisherman. Hūs is not in the active prior lexicon and must be supplied.

support_groups.local_meaning: And set before him the provisions that he had to offer him.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply ēstas, lęgde, dative him beforan, object-relative ðe, and the available-to-offer habban construction. Tō bēodanne morphology is new Unit6, offer sense prior, but the object/recipient availability frame remains supplied. The second him is Apollonius, not a reflexive recipient.

support_groups.local_meaning: He still wanted, according to his ability, to show him greater kindness.
support_groups.scope_note: Wolde + plain infinitive volition is new Unit6. Supply gīet, be his mihte, ārfæstnesse, and gecȳðan with accusative thing shown/dative recipient. Mihte here is a noun. No fact about prefix ge- or generalized government is inferred.

support_groups.local_meaning: He then tore his cloak in two.
support_groups.scope_note: Supply tōslāt, wǣfels and the entire on twā expression. The subject remains the fisherman; no new subordinate clause. Do not test the gender of an unexpressed noun or infer a general on+motion rule.
Prior giving frame; supply Apollonie, healfan dǣl. One half renders ðone healfan dǣl without inventing a second object.
Supply cweðende as a present participle accompanying the same subject, plus ðus. It is not a finite past or a command. No productive participial syntax is introduced.

support_groups.local_meaning: Take what I have to give you.
support_groups.scope_note: Nim is new singular imperative. Supply entire definite free-relative ðæt ic ... hæbbe and available-to-give construction. Sęllanne is new infinitive morphology; hæbbe uses prior indicative1sg in this reading, although its isolated surface is syncretic. Do not test a unique mood from the letters alone.

Gā is new singular imperative. Supply intō ðǣre ceastre as a whole destination phrase preserving its actual dative. This completes the first spoken sentence; subsequent source speech remains unassigned.
